gaps.note: The DCP-SC-28P user manual (14.0), Physical Description, lists one QSFP-DD probe port and says nothing else about it - no rate, no protocol, no supported optic; its power table only quotes figures with no QSFP-DD fitted.
gaps.wanted: what the probe port carries and at what rate, so the port can state a `speed` - or a media that says it is not an Ethernet interface.

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold

an `attrs.performance` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in a missing `attrs.power` section; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in a missing `attrs.environmental` section (profile `optical` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on port groups probe, rj45-1g, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: DCP-SC-28P User Manual - unit height is 1U (1.77 in); width and depth taken from the DCP-R chassis the family shares (440 x 505mm)

column-pitch.note: raw connection points jitter between 13.85 and 14.80mm, which put ports 7/9 and 8/10 into a 0.15mm overlap that lint L13 caught. Each RJ45 group is therefore fitted to a uniform pitch across its span - 14.32mm left, 14.34mm right - and the drawing jitter discarded

connector-choice.note: the ganged cell (common/rj45-ganged-eth@1, 12.7mm) is used rather than the single housing (common/rj45-eth@1, 15.8mm) because the measured 14.3mm column pitch cannot accommodate the latter

port-count.note: the recovered layout confirms the model name - 24 RJ45 on a 14.3mm column pitch plus 4 LC duplex, i.e. 28 ports, and a separate PROBE

port-families.note: DCP-SC-28P User Manual R14.0 A section 2.2 lists the shelf controller's ports as 1x RS232, 1x ETH0, 24x RJ-45 1G Ethernet, 4x SFP+ 10G Ethernet and 1x QSFP-DD probe. Its NEBS warnings address the RJ-45 block as ETH1-12 plus ETH17-28 and section 8.7 calls the optical pair ETH13-16, so the numbering is one 1-28 series with the SFP+ cages in the middle of it, not two rows. The front-view figure agrees - the cages sit two over two between the RJ45 blocks, under silkscreen boxes reading 13/14 and 15/16

port-identification.note: RJ45 columns carry one connection point per port; the LC columns carry two about 6.4mm apart, one per fiber, which is what distinguishes them

port-positions.note: stencil ShapeSheet connection points, stored by Visio as fractions of shape width/height and resolved against the 19-inch rack width

probe-port.note: QSFP-DD, from the same list. Measured off the front-view figure against the RJ45 height it is about 19.7 x 10.6mm, i.e. a QSFP-family cage and not the SFP+ one an earlier revision drew. Placed on the centre the stencil recovered, so only the aperture changed

psu-orientation.note: photo - both modules are fitted the same way round, fan inboard of the inlet, so the C14 sits at the far right on PSU-2 and inboard on PSU-1. They are not mirrored

psu-part.note: label - Gospower G1251-0550WNA, P/N CRPS0550-AH, and the fan sticker reads 550W Platinum CRPS. So the module is a standard CRPS 1U part at 73.5 x 40 x 185, not the 84mm-wide estimate taken from the racked photo, and both bays sit flush to the chassis edges

rear-layout.note: photo IMG_2181 of racked DCP-R units - PSU with integrated fan and C14 inlet at each end, mirrored; honeycomb vent panel across the centre; management block right of centre. Block positions are approximate to about 3mm - the photo has uncorrected perspective and partial cable occlusion, so it fixes the structure and order but not exact millimetres

rear-mgmt-block.note: none. The SC-28P carries no rear management ports - its manual places only power and fan units in the back panel, and its ETH0 and RS232 are on the front. An earlier revision copied the DCP-R rear here by mistake; the vent now spans what that block wrongly occupied

sfp-media.note: SFP+ 10G, from the same list. The stencil could only show LC duplex because the figure's cages are fitted with LC optics; the cage itself is SFP+ and the ports are now modelled as such rather than as the bare `sfp` family token

side-top-bottom.note: IMG_2188 shows the lid, so these now carry the real finish - a light silver body with the black front panel wrapping about 12.7mm (half an inch) back along every face. Still no vents, screws or lid labels - the photo shows the finish and the panel depth but not those details, so they are left out rather than invented

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 2 SFP pairs (port-13/port-14 and port-15/port-16).
